conditions.name: fast SMA crosses above slow SMA

entry_rule.rule_text: fast SMA crosses above slow SMA (fast=10, slow=50) AND MACD line above signal

interpretation: A pure trend-following trigger (fast SMA crosses above slow SMA (fast=10, slow=50)) with no additional regime filter -- expect more false signals in sideways markets, offset (if the edge holds) by larger average winners when a real trend does follow. Risk model: stop at 0.99x ATR from entry, target at 5.00R (i.e. 4.95x ATR), max hold 18 bars, entries filled at the next bar's open to avoid lookahead. Realized: 31 trades, 58% win rate (Wilson 95% lower bound 41%), reward:risk 3.93, expectancy +1.86R/trade, profit factor 5.44. In this sample both win rate and reward:risk pull their weight here -- a robust, 'high win-rate AND high R:R' combination rather than leaning on one factor. Out-of-sample check: 14 trades, 36% win rate, expectancy +0.44R -- does NOT clearly hold out of sample; treat as unvalidated.

A standalone mean-reversion entry (RSI oversold (period=14, threshold=33.6)) with no trend filter -- this is the riskiest archetype here, since it will also fire against strong downtrends. Its edge, if real, likely comes from a high win rate on quick reversion trades rather than trend participation. Risk model: stop at 1.75x ATR from entry, target at 2.48R (i.e. 4.34x ATR), max hold 26 bars, entries filled at the next bar's open to avoid lookahead. Realized: 30 trades, 73% win rate (Wilson 95% lower bound 56%), reward:risk 2.40, expectancy +1.28R/trade, profit factor 6.61. In this sample both win rate and reward:risk pull their weight here -- a robust, 'high win-rate AND high R:R' combination rather than leaning on one factor. Out-of-sample check: 18 trades, 56% win rate, expectancy +0.88R -- holds up out of sample.

A standalone participation filter (volume above its average (mult=1.66)) used as the entry trigger itself, with nothing else gating it -- above-average volume alone says nothing about direction, so this rule is really asking 'is something happening' rather than 'should I be long', and its edge (if any) most likely reflects a general tendency for high-volume bars to precede continuation in this data. Risk model: stop at 2.75x ATR from entry, target at 4.95R (i.e. 13.61x ATR), max hold 59 bars, entries filled at the next bar's open to avoid lookahead. Realized: 37 trades, 73% win rate (Wilson 95% lower bound 57%), reward:risk 4.09, expectancy +2.25R/trade, profit factor 11.05. In this sample both win rate and reward:risk pull their weight here -- a robust, 'high win-rate AND high R:R' combination rather than leaning on one factor. Out-of-sample check: 21 trades, 33% win rate, expectancy +0.48R -- does NOT clearly hold out of sample; treat as unvalidated.
